record.original_question: If an abelian prodiscrete group is compactly generated and compact-free, meaning that it has no nontrivial compact subgroups, must it be a finitely generated free abelian group?

evidence.quote: Question 8. Is a compactly generated abelian prodiscrete compact–free group a finitely generated free abelian group? Note that by compact-free we mean the group has no nontrivial compact subgroups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a Hausdorff topological abelian group. Call $G$ prodiscrete if it is complete and the open subgroups of $G$ form a neighborhood basis of $0$ (equivalently, $G$ is an inverse limit of discrete abelian groups). Call $G$ compactly generated if there exists a compact subset $K \subseteq G$ such that $G$ is algebraically generated by $K$. Call $G$ compact-free if $G$ contains no nontrivial compact subgroup.

Question: Must every compactly generated, compact-free, prodiscrete abelian topological group be isomorphic (as a topological group) to a finitely generated free abelian group $\mathbb{Z}^n$ (with the discrete topology)?
artifact.status_search_result: Known structural results (Hofmann–Morris) show that any compactly generated, compact-free prodiscrete abelian group embeds as a closed subgroup of some power $\mathbb{Z}^J$, but searches do not surface a published proof or counterexample to the stronger claim that such a group must be a finitely generated free abelian group. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The structure of abelian pro-Lie groups (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Any compactly generated, compact-free prodiscrete group is isomorphic to a closed subgroup of a group Z^J.
status_evidence.claim: Closed-subgroup-of-Z^J embedding is the best general structural result available; full identification with a finitely generated free abelian group is not established.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on compactly generated prodiscrete abelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: Question concerning whether a compactly generated abelian prodiscrete compact-free group must be a finitely generated free abelian group.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open question, with no resolution found in subsequent literature searches.
